x-research-tools.description: Offline development utility, separate from the whatsapp-cli control API; no HTTP route. Decodes complete protobuf-lite descriptors with variable-width scalar-presence and repeated entries, UTF-16 integer continuation/overflow checks, header/count validation and exact field-name pairing. Excludes bitFieldN_ bookkeeping names. Unsupported oneof mapping, malformed/truncated input, ambiguous descriptors or name mismatches are diagnosed on stderr without printing a partial pairing. Existing utility parameters remain positional APK and required --class. APK 2.26.37.71 BX5 mixes repeated strings and scalar int64 fields; fixed-triple decoding was refuted. BZc still decodes all 110 Message fields.

info.title: TeleWhatsApp control API
info.description: This document describes every operation of the whatsapp-api library and whatsapp-cli. The x-transport field indicates whether an operation is served by whatsapp-cli serve over HTTP today or invoked through the CLI. The x-cli field gives the exact command. The x-library field names the Rust entry points behind each operation (crate path form); the whatsapp-cli test `openapi_library_symbols_exist` verifies they exist. The x-live field marks operations that contact WhatsApp servers and require explicit authorization via --allow-live-request. The HTTP control plane has no authentication and binds to loopback only.

fresh_sessions.description: Discard the saved Signal session with each recipient device and establish a new one from a fresh prekey bundle, keeping the pinned peer identity (a changed identity is still refused). skdm_delivery.description: Group send only: how the sender key is distributed. `participants` (default) puts one `<enc>` per device inside the group stanza's `<participants>`; `direct` sends one ordinary direct message per device carrying the distribution, before the group stanza, and omits `<participants>` entirely. Both are real — `includeSenderKeysInMessage` is a per-send flag in SendE2EMessageJob and SendLiveLocationKeyJob distributes keys entirely out of band.

mark_read.description: During a messaging session (`listen`), send a read receipt for every incoming direct or group message with readable content (Message fields 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 26 or 66) that decrypts. Sender-key distributions, protocol messages and reactions get none. Each receipt goes through the same durable, once-only queue as `mark-read`. Applies to `listen` and to `lab-transport --receive`. Off by default: the official client marks messages read when a chat is on screen, which this client cannot infer. Applies to eligible authenticated duplicates on redelivery too, including offline recovery; durable read markers prevent repetitions after uncertain writes or ACKs.

identity_changes.description: Incoming remote prekey trust policy for listen and lab receive. pinned refuses changed saved identities. apk_authenticated permits replacement only after nested message authentication, atomically archiving the prior pin/session and emitting IdentityChanged with the inbox commit. It does not establish human verification. Own-device messages remain pinned. Outgoing bundle replacement has a separate opt-in outgoing_identity_changes; uncertain sends never replay.

outgoing_identity_changes.description: Independent outgoing remote directory-bundle policy for the normal comparison outbox. Pinned suspends changed identities. Apk_authenticated requires a valid signed device key received through authenticated Noise, derives a fresh peer session, archives prior pin/session with signed_directory_bundle provenance and emits IdentityChanged atomically with the original send reservation. Own-account identities remain pinned. It is not human verification. Incoming identity_changes does not enable this. Unknown/refused queries and uncertain sends never resume. Repeating the original outbox-send JSON may resolve an identity-suspended intent using its saved reply; no new query or intent ID is created. General listen --send-outbox does not select suspended intents. Suspensions without an observed pin snapshot cannot resume, and stale replies cannot roll a newer current peer pin back.

post.summary: Decrypt captured direct replies locally, without network I/O
post.description: Decrypt authenticated incoming records locally. The operation is offline. Saved-payload inspection labels Message field 102 as message-history-notice and shows only its nested field numbers, grounded in APK 2.26.37.71 BZc/BV6.dynamicMethod. Metadata values remain redacted; history is not fetched or applied. Poll inspection reports question/option byte lengths and counts, selectable count and secret-presence; it no longer prints question or option text. Unknown nested fields remain visible, and malformed nested protobuf fails inspection. This label does not establish sender authorization, history availability, or synchronization completion. With `inspect: true`, display the plaintext protobuf structure without advancing sessions. With replay_captures, preserved message captures are re-run through inbox::process offline to recover stanzas that an earlier defect refused; this is how the first live group messages were recovered after the sender-key distribution field number was corrected. With --inspect, prekey_pin_matches compares the first pkmsg public identity to saved comparison-direct pins for from, sender_pn, participant and participant_pn aliases. Some(true) means matching, Some(false) means differing, None means no saved pin; invalid_input marks malformed inspection data, and invalid_ciphertext marks a non-byte pkmsg payload. This is offline, read-only, prints no keys or full addresses, does not authenticate the ciphertext and does not authorize a pin replacement. Signal failures report fixed redacted categories rather than underlying address/backend strings. --accept-authenticated-identity-changes requires --replay-captures and conflicts with --inspect. It explicitly selects APK-compatible incoming remote key changes after successful authentication. Previous pins/sessions are archived, an IdentityChanged event is emitted atomically with the inbox/session/prekey commit, and no receipt or network request is sent. Default remains pinned. This is not human verification; no safety-number algorithm is claimed. Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Cleared and consumed rows are skipped rather than failing the run. Also prints the per-class counts on offline/offline_preview stanzas (message, receipt, status, notification, appdata, call), which is how to tell whether the server ever queued a given class of stanza for this account at all.

post.summary: One comparison-server connection; optional bounded primary login
post.description: Establish a single connection to the comparison server (x-live) with optional bounded primary login, message transmission, or receive mode. A successful login records this account's own LID from the `<success>` stanza, which a LID-addressed group names us by. When the message JSON carries `group` instead of `to`, the send is a sender-key fan-out: a `w:g2` info query resolves the membership, a `usync devices` query resolves each member's devices, `encrypt` supplies bundles for devices without a session, and one `<message>` carries a per-device `<enc>` distribution inside `<participants>` beside the group `skmsg`. It refuses rather than sending when a member has no device list. After any send the connection is held briefly and whatever the server sends next is preserved, because a recipient that cannot decrypt answers with a `receipt type="retry"` naming the failing device. A `<success>` or `<failure>` login result is preserved too: a `<failure>` carries an `appeal_token` and a refusal cannot be replayed to fetch one again. Receive mode shares listen’s durable once-only decryption-failure retry queue; no repeated count=1 requests after redelivery or uncertain writes. Inspect with receipts (offline). Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. When mark_read is enabled, eligible authenticated duplicates recovered offline also enter the once-only read queue on redelivery. The helper checks the saved decrypted readable payload; cleared/consumed rows and protocol-only content are skipped. A write-cut regression verifies uncertain reads are never replayed.

login.description: Send one primary login after certificate verification

receive.description: Preserve incoming stanzas for up to 30 seconds without sending a chat. Incoming `presence` and `chatstate` stanzas are reported (redacted) as they arrive.

media_route.description: Obtain and privately preserve one current media-upload route response

message.description: Private JSON: request_id, either to (direct) or group (`…@g.us` fan-out), and text, image (PNG) or voice_note (Ogg/Opus); a group send is text only so far

recheck_refusal.description: Authorize exactly one further login after a saved `failure`, to tell a temporary limit from a permanent refusal. Requires a saved `failure` (never an ambiguous `outcome_unknown`), refuses to carry a message, and preserves the earlier refusal under its own key instead of overwriting it.

push_name.description: Set the display name others see beside this number: one `<presence name=… type="available"/>` after login (comparison 2.26.37.71 `LX/0y0->A00`, `WriterThread/write/push-name`, confirmed). Fire-and-forget: the server sends no reply, so the CLI reports `written`, not accepted, and records it under the `push-name` checkpoint. The 100-character bound is this client's; the APK enforces none on the wire. Not live-verified yet.

typing.description: Show a typing indicator in this chat (E.164 digits, a phone/LID JID or a `…@g.us` group): announces `presence type=available`, writes `<chatstate to=…><composing/></chatstate>` (`LX/B2G->A01`, confirmed), holds for `typing_seconds` without reading (a cancelled read closes this channel), then writes `<paused/>` (`LX/B2H->handleMessage`, confirmed). Combined with `message`, the indicator runs before the send. Not live-verified yet.

typing_state.description: `recording` is `composing media="audio"` (shown while recording a voice note); `paused` writes only the stop.

subscribe.description: During `receive`, subscribe to these people's availability and typing, as opening their chat does: after activation, `presence type=available`, then per person `<presence type="subscribe" to=…>` with a `<tctoken>` child carrying their saved trusted-contact token when one is held (comparison 2.26.37.71 `LX/0y0->A00`, `WriterThread/write/subscription-request`, confirmed; token bound 1..=120 bytes). Incoming `presence` (available/unavailable, `last` seen) and `chatstate` (composing/recording/paused) are then reported during the window with identities redacted. People only; group typing arrives without a subscription. Not live-verified yet.

post.summary: Maintain an authenticated comparison connection and process incoming messages
post.description: Establish an authenticated session to the messaging server (x-live). Hold the connection for the requested duration, receive incoming messages, and optionally transmit all eligible queued intents. Group messages (enc type=skmsg) are decrypted when a SenderKeyDistributionMessage for the (group, sender) pair has been received in a prior or current direct message; messages without a stored sender key are preserved as Unsupported without acknowledgement. SKDM distribution arrives embedded in pkmsg/msg payloads (WhatsApp Message field 2), either standalone or as a second enc child of the group stanza, and is committed atomically with the inbox row. A decrypted group message is confirmed with a receipt addressed to the group carrying the sender as participant. Status updates (from=status@broadcast) route through the same sender-key path and project into a Broadcast chat with the poster as sender, but are never confirmed with a receipt: the status receipt shape (class=status, type=sender) has an unresolved sts input, so none is sent. Each incoming stanza except keepalive replies is reported on stderr as one redacted `incoming` log line (element, type, chat class, enc types, inbox outcome, confirmed, marked_read); this is the default when RUST_LOG is unset. On Undecryptable incoming messages, queues a retry receipt using the saved Signal registration ID. Both listen and lab receive use one request per chat/participant/message ID, durably reserved before transmission; repeats and uncertain outcomes never reset it. This is a conservative client policy, not an APK retry limit. Missing registration or unsupported routing is logged without ending receive; storage failures propagate. The receipts command inspects outcomes offline. Live 2026-10-06: saved-account login and activation succeeded; one automatic retry received a matching server ACK. Its redelivery still failed decryption, and fresh-message automatic read validation remains pending. Signal failure diagnostics classify missing keys, untrusted identity, bad MAC, duplicate counter and invalid encoding without printing peer addresses or backend details. This does not explain the historical window with no incoming message stanzas. Offline preserved-capture inspection found incoming prekey identities differing from both saved PN and LID pins; no pin was replaced. Human safety-number verification is not implemented, and the underlying cause of the saved mismatch remains unknown. Explicit authenticated incoming replacement is available as described below. Direct and group pairwise prekey processing persists first-seen differing public-key fingerprints; identity-conflicts inspects these unauthenticated observations offline. Pins and sessions are not replaced. A failing direct Signal child within a group stanza is also Undecryptable and eligible for the same once-only retry; missing sender-key/session support remains Unsupported. transport.identity_changes explicitly selects pinned (default) or apk_authenticated; the latter atomically archives old remote keys/sessions and emits IdentityChanged after message authentication. Local/own-device identities are not replaced. Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. When mark_read is enabled, eligible authenticated duplicates recovered offline also enter the once-only read queue on redelivery. The helper checks the saved decrypted readable payload; cleared/consumed rows and protocol-only content are skipped. A write-cut regression verifies uncertain reads are never replayed. Live 2026-10-07: a 45-second session delivery-confirmed the two recovered direct/group messages as duplicates. A subsequent 20-second session server-acknowledged both explicitly queued saved-message reads; eight reads and one retry are now acknowledged. Handset blue ticks and fresh-message automatic reads remain unconfirmed.

This differs from contacts check only in mode and context: check sends query/interactive for a single number, which is discovery rather than address-book registration. allow_mutation is deliberately not emitted because what enables it is unknown. Offline: the request is queued on the durable action queue and a later session transmits it. Whether registering contacts affects Status delivery is unknown and untested; see docs/protocol/status.md.

contacts.description: How many saved contacts the sync includes.

post.summary: Queue a read-only app-state fetch for every collection (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Ask the server for each app-state collection's snapshot at version 0 (CSe.A00/CSe.A01: <sync data_namespace=3><collection name order version=0 return_snapshot="true"/>). Read-only: no <patch> child is emitted, since CSe.A01 adds it only when a patch argument is present. The reply carries the server's authoritative version per collection, which patch writing needs because patches must be strictly sequential. Live 2026-09-22: accepted, and the reply was an empty <sync/>, confirming this account holds no app state.

post.summary: Queue an app-state contactAction patch publishing every saved contact (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Build and queue a SyncdPatch of contactAction SET mutations, one per saved contact, into the critical_unblock_low collection (LX/Azs->A00 routes contactAction there, confirmed — not a 'regular' collection). Index is ["contact", <jid>] and SyncActionData.version is 2, both confirmed from LX/B6M. Mints this device's app-state key if it has none. The <collection version> attribute is the version the client currently holds and is omitted for a never-synced collection (confirmed, CSe.A01 call sites). LIVE STATUS: refused. Two attempts, both answered iq type=error code=400 text=bad-request; the second carried the corrected version semantics. Not iterated further. See docs/protocol/chat-actions.md for the undistinguished candidates.

Keeps the attempt id, its identity, its keys and its history; creates no new attempt; honours the challenge handle's retry_after; and refuses any state other than a pending challenge. This is the official client's resend, not a restart.

Receipts are kept at the furthest state a viewer reached, so a delivery replayed from an offline queue cannot demote a view. Reading this sends nothing and emits no read receipt.

parameters.description: Only this status, by wire id

Each child is included only when supplied, so setting a PIN cannot clear the recovery address as a side effect, and an empty code turns two-step verification off. The PIN is read from redirected stdin, never a command-line argument, and is never echoed or logged. Distinct from `lab-signup verify-pin`, which answers a PIN challenge rather than changing the PIN. Offline: a session transmits the queued action.

This is how the account's other devices learn the name; other people see it through the separate `<presence name=…>` stanza sent by `lab-transport --push-name`. Builds on the collection state the server last accepted and promotes the new state only once the server accepts it; a 409 conflict is caught up from the returned patches. Offline: a session such as `listen` transmits the queued action. Live 2026-09-25: accepted, `<collection name="critical_block" version="1"/>`.

name.description: The display name; trimmed; 100 characters is this client's bound, not WhatsApp's

An empty text is sent as a single space, as `LX/8lM->A04` does. The 256-character bound is this client's; the writer enforces none and the screen's own limit was not traced. Offline: a session such as `listen` transmits the queued action and records the reply.

get.summary: Inspect durable peer identity conflict observations offline
get.description: Lists first-seen SHA-256 public-key fingerprint differences observed in incoming prekey envelopes. These observations are unauthenticated: they do not establish a legitimate identity change, replace a pin, advance a session, clear verification, or authorize sending. The peer address is represented by a local SHA-256 selector. Replay/redelivery of the same peer/pinned/observed combination preserves the original timestamp. CLI only; no HTTP route exists.

get.summary: Inspect queued sends suspended by changed peer identities (offline, redacted)
get.description: Lists identity-mismatch suspensions without contacts, keys, payloads or network requests. Intents remain queued under their original local IDs; the saved key-query reply and reservation remain encrypted. The static reason distinguishes identity_changed from invalid_signed_bundle and own_identity_pinned. Inspection performs no replacement or replay; selected outbox-send can resolve a valid saved reply under the independent outgoing policy. This contract is implemented by the CLI only.

get.summary: Inspect saved primary PN/LID peer pin and session agreement (offline)
get.description: Reads one logical snapshot without queries, key replacement or sends. Requires a primary phone-number chat JID. Returns hashed peer selectors, diagnostic public-key fingerprints, held-session/pin agreement, and all authenticated primary LID mappings. A qualifying saved incoming transition establishes local provenance only; it is not a WhatsApp safety number or human verification. Store opening can commit engine metadata; protocol records are inspected read-only. No HTTP route is implemented.

parameters.name: chat
parameters.description: Primary phone-number chat JID (private input, never printed in the result).

post.summary: Queue or inspect one peer directory key query (offline)
post.description: peer-keys queues a normal encrypt/key IQ on the existing once-only action queue; listen transmits it over authenticated Noise. Repeated queueing returns the original action ID locally. --show inspects the latest saved result and current PN/LID pin matches without adopting a key, deriving a session or sending a chat. --refresh is explicit and permitted only after a successful valid signed prior bundle; all old replies remain encrypted. Queued, uncertain, refused, invalid and missing prior queries cannot be refreshed. Output omits peer addresses, public key bytes and raw server error text. Fingerprints are SHA-256 diagnostics, not safety numbers or human verification. This is CLI-only; no HTTP route exists.

parameters.name: chat
parameters.description: Primary phone-number chat JID (private input, never printed in the result).

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: Inspect saved evidence without queueing. Mutually exclusive with refresh.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Explicitly queue a new request only after verified successful prior evidence. Mutually exclusive with show.

200.description: Original action selector, saved redacted inspection, or null when no query exists

action_id.description: Original one-shot action selector; repeated queueing reuses it.
